key_insight: MAPS uses a centralized continuous "proto-plan" to coordinate decentralized vehicle control, separating global strategy from local execution for better multi-agent intersection handling.
engineering_relevance: This architecture offers a practical way to scale autonomous vehicle coordination at unsignalized intersections while improving safety, travel time, and zero-shot generalization across agent counts.
method: Master agent produces a compact latent proto-plan for global coordination.
Worker agents combine the proto-plan with local observations for vehicle-level control.
Hierarchical design supports independent optimization of strategy and tactics.
evidence_signal: Evaluated in HighwayEnv across 72 intersection configurations, MAPS achieved collision-free navigation, reduced average travel time, and reached a 94% success rate when trained with three agents and deployed zero-shot to five agents.
watch_item: Results are shown in simulation, so real-world performance may depend on sensing noise, traffic uncertainty, and transfer to physical vehicles.
paper_title: Compact Latent Coordination for Autonomous Vehicles at Unsignalized Intersections
